title: What Should an Experiment Measure? Combining a Short-Term Experiment with Confounded Observational Data to Identify Long-Term Treatment Effects
abstract: arXiv:2611.30599v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Observational data often record long-term outcomes but do not identify long-term treatment effects when selection depends on unrecorded characteristics, while randomized experiments remove this selection but require years of follow-up. We ask what a short-term experiment should measure so that, combined with observational data, it identifies the average long-term treatment effect in the observational population. In our main setting, the observational data record a coarse post-treatment measurement of the unrecorded characteristics but not a detailed measurement that would remove confounding. In this setting, we derive three implications for what the experiment should measure. translated_title: 实验应该测量什么？结合短期实验与存在混杂的观察性数据以识别长期处理效应
translated_abstract: 观察性数据通常记录长期结果，但当选择机制依赖于未被记录的特征时，观察性数据无法识别长期处理效应；而随机实验可以消除这种选择偏差，却需要多年的随访。我们探讨短期实验应当测量什么，才能与观察性数据相结合，识别出观察人群中的平均长期处理效应。在我们的主要设定中，观察性数据记录了对这些未记录特征的粗略处理后测量，但未记录能够消除混杂的详细测量。在这一设定下，我们推导出关于实验应测量什么的三个结论。实验应当：(1) 收集相同的粗略测量；(2) 以足够的细节测量这些特征，使得在给定该详细测量和已记录协变量的条件下能够消除混杂，并使粗略测量对选择和处理……
tldr: 该论文提出一个理论框架，指出短期实验应测量哪些变量，才能与存在混杂的观察性数据结合后识别出观察人群中的长期处理效应。
en_tdlr: This paper derives what a short-term experiment should measure so that, when combined with confounded observational data, it can identify long-term treatment effects in the observational population.
